title: Impact of MRI modality selection on glioma sub-region segmentation using 3D U-Net and Attention U-Net: A comparative evaluation across ten MRI sequences

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Impact of MRI modality selection on glioma sub-region segmentation using 3D U-Net and Attention U-Net: A comparative evaluation across ten MRI sequences》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background · p0030】Rather than developing a combined multiparametric segmentation pipeline, the central aim of this study was to identify, for each glioma subregion, the single MRI weighting associated with the best segmentation performance, an objective that requires each modality to be evaluated independently. In this study, we aim to address this gap by conducting a comparative evaluation of the contribution of individual MRI sequences to glioma subregion semantic segmentation, using standard U-Net and Attention U-Net architectures trained independently on structural MRI sequences (T1, T2, FLAIR, and T1Gd), DWI modalities (DWI, ADC map, FA, and MD), as well as SWI and ASL.

【Background · p0010】Gliomas are the most common primary malignant tumors of the central nervous system and are characterized by highly infiltrative growth patterns and substantial biological heterogeneity [1]. These tumors often comprise distinct subregions, including peritumoral edema, necrotic core, and actively proliferating tumor tissue, each of which carries important diagnostic and prognostic significance [2]. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the standard modality for the noninvasive assessment of gliomas subregions, offering diverse imaging contrasts that reflect anatomical structure as well as underlying diffusion, perfusion, and susceptibility properties [3,4]. Accurate identification, segmentation, and delineation of glioma subregions are essential for treatment planning, radiotherapy targeting, and longitudinal monitoring of disease progression [5].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Impact of MRI modality selection on glioma sub-region segmentation using 3D U-Net and Attention U-Net: A comparative evaluation across ten MRI sequences》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · abstract-2-1】A total of 468 subjects from the UCSF-PDGM dataset were included. Ten MRI weightings were assessed independently: apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, arterial spin labeling (ASL), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), fractional anisotropy (FA), mean diffusivity (MD), susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI), T1-weighted, T1-weighted post-contrast (T1Gd), FLAIR, and T2-weighted imaging. For each modality, dedicated 3D U-Net and 3D Attention U-Net models were trained. TOPSIS multi-criteria ranking was applied to identify optimal model-modality combinations per sub-region and overall.

【Material and methods · p0035】In this study, we present a deep learning–based framework for the automated semantic segmentation of glioma subregions using multiparametric MRI. A diverse set of MRI sequences was incorporated to capture complementary structural, diffusion, perfusion, and susceptibility information, including structural MRI image-weights (T1-weighted, T2-weighted, FLAIR, and T1Gd), diffusion-based modalities (DWI, ADC map, FA map, and MD map), as well as SWI and ASL. Two convolutional neural network architectures, standard U-Net and Attention U-Net, were employed to perform voxel-wise segmentation of clinically relevant glioma subregions, namely peritumoral edema, necrotic core, and active tumor tissue. An overview of the proposed methodological workflow is illustrated in Fig. 1.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Impact of MRI modality selection on glioma sub-region segmentation using 3D U-Net and Attention U-Net: A comparative evaluation across ten MRI sequences》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Model performance evaluation · p0105】TOPSIS operates by identifying a Positive Ideal Solution (A⁺), representing the hypothetically best attainable values across all criteria, and a Negative Ideal Solution (A⁻), representing the worst. Each combination is then ranked by its relative closeness to A⁺ and distance from A⁻, expressed through a Closeness Coefficient (CC). The TOPSIS procedure was implemented in six steps. First, a decision matrix X of dimensions 20 × 3 was constructed for each sub-region, where rows correspond to model–modality combinations and columns correspond to the three-evaluation metrics. Second, the matrix was normalized using vector (L2) normalization to eliminate scale differences between metrics: rᵢⱼ = xᵢⱼ / √(Σx²ᵢⱼ). Third, a weighted normalized matrix was obtained by multiplying each normalized value by its assigned criterion weight wⱼ: vᵢⱼ = wⱼ · rᵢⱼ. Equal weights (w=1/3 for DSC, IoU, and HD95) were assigned to all evaluation criteria, reflecting the absence of an a priori basis for prioritizing overlap-based accuracy over boundary-based accuracy in glioma sub-region segmentation and avoiding the introduction of subjective bias into the ranking (to assess the robustness of the resulting rankings to this weighting choice, a sensitivity analysis was subsequently performed under alternative weighting schemes in the supplementary file). Fourth, the ideal solutions were determined. For benefit criteria (DSC, IoU), A⁺ was defined as the maximum weighted normalized value per criterion and A⁻ as the minimum. For the cost criterion HD95, this convention was inverted: A⁺(HD95) = min(vᵢⱼ) and A⁻(HD95) = max(vᵢⱼ), reflecting the fact that lower HD95 values indicate better boundary accuracy. Fifth, the Euclidean separation distances from the positive and negative ideal solutions were computed for each combination: S⁺ᵢ = √Σ(vᵢⱼ − v⁺ⱼ)² and S⁻ᵢ = √Σ(vᵢⱼ − v⁻ⱼ)². Sixth, the Closeness Coefficient was derived as CCᵢ = S⁻ᵢ / (S⁺ᵢ + S⁻ᵢ), yielding a value in the range [0, 1] where a value approaching 1 indicates near-ideal performance. All 20 combinations were ranked by CCᵢ in descending order, and the combination achieving the highest CC was identified as the optimal model for the respective sub-region.

【Model performance evaluation · p0110】To evaluate the stability of the TOPSIS-based modality rankings to the choice of criterion weights, a sensitivity analysis was performed. In addition to the uniform weighting scheme used in the primary analysis (wDSC=wIoU=wHD95=1/3), three alternative weighting schemes were tested, each assigning greater emphasis to a single criterion: (i) DSC-emphasized (wDSC=0.6, wIoU=0.2, wHD95=0.2), (ii) IoU-emphasized (wDSC=0.2, wIoU=0.6, wHD95=0.2), and (iii) HD95-emphasized (wDSC=0.2, wIoU=0.2, wHD95=0.6). TOPSIS closeness coefficients and rankings were recalculated for all 20 model–modality combinations per sub-region under each weighting scheme.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Impact of MRI modality selection on glioma sub-region segmentation using 3D U-Net and Attention U-Net: A comparative evaluation across ten MRI sequences》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Fig. 1 · fig0005】Fig. 1 Overview of the proposed workflow for MRI–based glioma subregion segmentation. Multi-weight MRI images, including ADC, ASL, DWI, FA, FLAIR, MD, SWI, T1, T1Gd, and T2, are first preprocessed and used for network training. Standard U-Net and Attention U-Net architectures are then trained to perform voxel-wise semantic segmentation of glioma subregions, namely edema, necrotic core, and active tumor tissue.

【Fig. 2 · fig0010】Fig. 2 Detailed architecture of the U-Net model used for glioma subregion segmentation. The network follows a symmetric encoder–decoder design with skip connections to preserve spatial information. Convolutional blocks (C1–C9, labeled A) consist of two 3 × 3 × 3 convolutional layers each, with the number of feature maps indicated in red next to each block. Pooling blocks (P1–P4, labeled B) perform 2 × 2 × 2 max-pooling for spatial downsampling in the encoder path. Upsampling blocks (U1–U4, labeled C) use transposed convolutions for upsampling, with the number of feature maps shown in red, and concatenate corresponding encoder features via skip connections. The final 1 × 1 × 1 convolution with SoftMax activation generates voxel-wise segmentation maps for edema, necrotic core, and active tumor regions.

【Fig. 3 · fig0015】Fig. 3 Architecture of the Attention U-Net used for glioma subregion segmentation. Convolutional blocks (C1–C9) each contain two 3 × 3 × 3 convolutional layers, with feature map numbers indicated in red. Pooling blocks (P1–P4) perform 2 × 2 × 2 max-pooling for downsampling. Upsampling blocks (U1–U4) use transposed convolutions for upsampling and concatenate with encoder features. Attention blocks (A1–A4) are applied at each skip connection, and consist of 1 × 1 × 1 convolutions for encoder and decoder inputs, batch normalization, element-wise addition, ReLU activation, 1 × 1 × 1 convolution, and a sigmoid gating function to produce an attention map that weights the encoder features before concatenation. The final 1 × 1 × 1 convolution with SoftMax activation generates voxel-wise segmentation maps for edema, necrotic core, and active tumor regions.
